solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plants are having stems, therefore needing to be pinned

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

indicators.note: something pinned is held fast between other things, so this word sits held inside the stems

parts.note: canes are plant stems
thus means therefore

explanation.surface: A botanist notes that certain plants have stems that must be pinned to stay upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' looks like a verb but is the unit of area, one hundred square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a genus of spiny-leaved perennials, so the plural names a group of such growing things.

clue.text: Copper to advertise safety device

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to tout is to advertise or promote

explanation.surface: A police officer promotes a piece of safety equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman; here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutout is a switch that breaks an electrical circuit automatically to prevent overload.

clue.text: Particular opening's marked by song in the Netherlands

indicators.note: in places the song inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: NL is the international code for the Netherlands
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A certain Dutch opening night is celebrated with song.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is possessive in sense: the answer is the adjective for one specific opening, the nostril.
explanation.definitionFit: Narial means relating to the nostrils, which are a particular opening in the body.

clue.text: Got hold of by Bob in Perth, I acted like a lout

indicators.note: to be got hold of is to be gripped, so the first word sits inside the second

parts.note: hod is a Scots word for bob, and Perth is in Scotland
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man in Perth confesses that, once Bob grabbed him, he behaved like a hooligan.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth looks Australian, where hoon is slang, but it is the Scottish city, flagging a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoon is Australian slang for behaving like a loutish hooligan, especially driving recklessly.

clue.text: Superior officer meets foreign friend turning up in den in garden?

parts.note: U means upper-class, socially superior
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A senior officer meets a friend from abroad in a garden hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'den in garden' looks like a shed; it means the final syllable of the word garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The ultima is the last syllable of a word, and den closes the word garden, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Use this chemical compound next in novel experiment

indicators.note: novel means new, so the long word is a remade arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters added alongside the answer

explanation.surface: A chemist says to use this compound in the next new trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: the answer plus 'next', rearranged, makes experiment, so take next out of experiment and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An epimer is one of a pair of stereoisomers differing at only one asymmetric carbon atom, a type of molecule.

clue.text: Bring new development to old city and don't allow one to have buses running round

indicators.note: to have is to hold, so the rearranged vehicles enclose the rest
running round suggests movement and disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city
to ban is to not allow
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A planner develops an ancient city and refuses to let anyone run buses around it.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur is the Mesopotamian city of Abraham, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To suburbanise is to make an area suburban, building housing estates and commuter developments there.

clue.text: What's harvested sadly had to be ditched — go very hungry, as before

indicators.note: sadly means badly or wretchedly, so the remaining letters are disordered
ditched means thrown away, so those letters leave the longer word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A failed harvest had to be thrown away, leaving people famished as before.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterve is an obsolete form of starve, meaning to be famished, hence 'as before' marking the old usage.

clue.text: German chemist has a meal — fish

parts.note: Fritz Haber, German Nobel laureate in chemistry
to dine is to have a meal

explanation.surface: A German scientist sits down to a fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Haberdine is an old word for salted or dried cod, so the plural refers to preserved seafood.

clue.text: Maybe like organ passage with tweaking of a gut

indicators.note: tweaking means adjusting or twisting, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An organist adjusts a gut string, as if a passage might be improved by fiddling with an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is part of the letters to rearrange, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fugato describes music written in the imitative manner of a fugue, as an organ piece often is; 'Maybe' flags that it is one example.

clue.text: Foreign officers with inside information meeting challenge outside club

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: outside means the challenge goes round the weapon

parts.note: a dare is a challenge
a meri or mere is a Maori war club

explanation.surface: Police from abroad with secret knowledge confront a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a nightspot; it is the Maori weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The gendarmerie is the French armed police force, so it is a body of police officers abroad.

clue.text: The French place, a strange island

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
to place is to put
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes a French location as an odd island.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the flying island in Swift's Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Laputa is the fantastical floating island visited by Gulliver, peopled by absurd scientists, so it is a truly odd isle.

clue.text: Severe old people affected somehow by contact with insect

definitions.text: affected somehow by contact with insect

parts.note: stern means severe
O is the standard abbreviation for old
a tribe is a people

explanation.surface: Harsh elderly folk are somehow upset by touching a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a botanical term for flowers whose pollen is deposited on the underside of a visiting insect's thorax.
explanation.definitionFit: A sternotribe flower is pollinated when an insect's breastbone brushes it, so it is affected through insect contact.

clue.text: Serve salad spiced up with sauce

indicators.note: spiced up means livened and changed, so these letters are remixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook serves a salad livened up with dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa verde is an Italian green condiment of herbs, capers and oil, poured over food.

clue.text: Head giving audible refusals

indicators.note: audible means heard rather than read, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: nays are votes against

explanation.surface: A boss gives out loud refusals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a boss; it is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A naze is a headland or promontory, as in the Naze in Essex.

clue.text: Article about terrible ruler very unacceptable in a Greek location

indicators.note: the abbreviation for very is unwanted here, so it is struck out of the ruler's name

parts.note: the indefinite article
on means about, concerning
Ivan the Terrible, Tsar of Russia
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: An article on a dreadful tyrant is deemed quite unacceptable in some Greek place.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivan the Terrible loses his V, leaving IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Aonian is the adjective for Aonia, the region of Boeotia around Mount Helicon, so it means situated in that Greek region.

clue.text: What's odd in old company, looking back? Shut up!

indicators.note: looking back means the whole combination is read from right to left
in places the word for odd inside the name of the company

parts.note: EMI, the former British record company
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone reminisces about a strange old firm until told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up!' is not a demand for silence but an order to confine someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To immure is to wall in or imprison, so the imperative matches an order to lock someone away.

clue.text: Stopping short, come to river or lake

indicators.note: a thing stopping short does not reach its end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: to come to someone is to meet them
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A walker halts abruptly on reaching a river or lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river or lake' looks like a pair of options; the river supplies a letter and the lake is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Meer is an old spelling of mere, a word for a pond or small body of standing water.

clue.text: Weed became tainted

definitions.meaning: first meaning: urinated, of horses or cattle, a sense of stale as a verb
second meaning: went stale, lost freshness

explanation.surface: A garden plant went bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' looks like a noun for an unwanted plant but is the past tense of wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale as a verb means both to urinate (of livestock) and to grow flat or spoiled, so the past tense covers both.

clue.text: Advice before putting back sheets or mattress?

definitions.note: a two-word instruction rather than a noun
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the household tip to ventilate where you sleep before remaking it
second meaning: an inflatable thing to sleep on

explanation.surface: A housekeeping tip for remaking the bed, with a mattress in question.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is the advice itself: freshen the bed before the sheets go back on.
explanation.definitionFit: An airbed is an inflatable mattress, and split in two it is the imperative to ventilate one's bed.

clue.text: Embrace one getting cross, needing to gather support

indicators.note: to gather is to take in, so the cross holds the support within it

parts.note: a means one
a zo or dzo is a cross between a yak and a cow
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A person in a cross mood needs gathering in with supportive arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective for angry; it is the yak hybrid, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrazo is a Spanish embrace, the hug of greeting between friends.

clue.text: Graffiti in the gents showing actor

parts.note: bog is British slang for toilet; the gents is a men's lavatory
graffiti is a form of art

explanation.surface: Scrawl on a lavatory wall depicts a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: Graffiti in the gents is lavatory wall art, read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart was the Hollywood star of Casablanca, so he is a famous film performer.

clue.text: East End ghost maybe in old-style escapade

indicators.note: East End speech drops an initial aitch, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a ghost is one example of something that haunts

explanation.surface: A Cockney spook takes part in an old-fashioned adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End of London is Cockney territory, where speakers famously drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunter is an archaic word for adventure, so it is an exploit from bygone days.

clue.text: Thanks after measure is laid down in code of honour

indicators.note: after means the word for thanks follows the measure

parts.note: an omer is an ancient Hebrew measure of grain
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Gratitude after a measure is enshrined in a code of conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Omertà is the Mafia's rule of silence, a code forbidding members to inform on others.

clue.text: Gravedigger's therefore getting it wrong — one wild creature?

parts.note: the gravedigger in Hamlet mangles Latin ergo into argal
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gravedigger muddles his logic and stumbles upon some untamed beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The clown in Hamlet says 'argal' for ergo, meaning therefore.
explanation.definitionFit: The argali is a large wild sheep of the Asian mountains, so it is one example of an untamed animal.

clue.text: Idiot getting too much infatuated, as of old

parts.note: an ass is a fool
OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: A fool becomes excessively besotted, in an old-fashioned way.
explanation.definitionFit: Assott is a Spenserian word meaning besotted or made foolish, hence the archaic marker.

clue.text: Attack has a couple of characters turning up in Moroccan house

indicators.text: a couple of characters turning up
indicators.note: only two letters of the word flip, and in a down clue turning up means reading them from bottom to top

parts.note: a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: An assault involves some characters popping up in a house in Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of characters' are the middle two letters of the attack word, swapped round.
explanation.definitionFit: A riad is a traditional Moroccan townhouse built round an interior courtyard garden.

clue.text: Good knight embracing maiden possibly gets control

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the first pair surrounds the cricket term

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
N is the chess notation for knight
in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored

explanation.surface: A chivalrous knight hugging a young woman takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like a young woman; in cricket it is a set of six balls bowled without a run conceded.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern is to rule, to have power over something.

clue.text: Having more rows maybe in boat around island

indicators.note: around means the vessel wraps about the island's letter

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A boat with more rows of oars goes round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' suggests rowing a boat; it means lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Linier is the comparative of liny, meaning marked with lines, so it means bearing additional lines.

clue.text: Act involving three thousand outside university

indicators.note: outside means the large numeral wraps around the university's letter

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, three times
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A theatre production involves three thousand people outside a college.
explanation.definitionFit: To mumm is to perform in a mummers' play, a traditional folk drama, so it means to perform.

clue.text: Need, say, to get from 'ere

indicators.note: the apostrophe in 'ere shows a Cockney dropping the initial aitch, so the next word loses its aitch too

parts.note: e.g., for example, means say
hence means from here

explanation.surface: A Cockney explains what is needed to get away from this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ere is here with its aitch dropped, so hence becomes 'ence in the same accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Egence is an obsolete noun for necessity or want, related to exigence.

clue.text: Juniper to preserve outside home

indicators.note: outside means the word for preserve goes round the word for home

parts.note: to save is to preserve
in means at home

explanation.surface: A gardener wants to keep a juniper bush outside the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Savine or savin is a species of juniper shrub, Juniperus sabina, once used medicinally.

clue.text: Rash I sorted out in medical treatment

indicators.note: sorted out suggests putting things into a new order, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient says their skin rash was cleared up during treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted' belongs to the letters; only 'out' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthrodesis is a surgical procedure fusing the bones of a joint, a form of medical intervention.

clue.text: Having less rain than anywhere else, stride out

definitions.text: Having less rain than anywhere else

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Somewhere with the least rainfall is a fine place to stride out walking.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of dry describes the place with the lowest rainfall of all.

clue.text: Insist on providing very small amount for beggar?

parts.note: a reference to The Threepenny Opera, Brecht's version of The Beggar's Opera
P is the abbreviation for pence

explanation.surface: Someone demands that a beggar be given a pittance.
explanation.walkthrough: Three pence, written 3p, is a tiny sum; the beggar points to Brecht's Threepenny Opera, based on The Beggar's Opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Threep is a Scots verb meaning to maintain obstinately or argue a point, so it means to keep asserting.

clue.text: When in trouble, rangers eat ants

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Park rangers, when struggling for food, resort to eating insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergataners are wingless male ants resembling workers, so the word names a kind of these insects.
